subject: Hosted API Annual Commit: Volume discount proposal & packaging options
messages:
From: Tim Carson <tim.carson@acme-payments.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.li@acme-payments.com
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring annual commit tiers and discounts for Hosted API

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're evaluating committed pricing for token-heavy features (transactional receipts + fraud signals) across our USD and EU regions. High level questions:

- What commit tiers do you typically recommend for a payments platform with ~12M monthly active users?
- Rough per-token economics at 3 commit levels (starter / growth / enterprise) and how overage is priced
- Any flexibility on credits for unused commit or quarterly true-ups?

We'd like something we can budget for H2 planning and that reduces burst costs compared to on-demand.

Can you send an annual-level proposal we can review with procurement?

—Tim
Tim Carson
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Payments

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Tim Carson <tim.carson@acme-payments.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Exploring annual commit tiers and discounts for Hosted API

Tim —

Thanks — appreciate the context. Attached is a concise annual commit proposal and pricing playbook (summary PDF + SOW draft) tuned to transactional workloads. Key points up front:

- Suggested commit tiers:
  • Starter: 50M tokens/year (for pilot teams, small production) — 10% off list per-token
  • Growth: 1B tokens/year (typical scaling path) — 18% off list per-token
  • Enterprise: 5B tokens/year (high-volume mission-critical) — 28% off list per-token + reserved capacity guarantees

- Example per-token economics (list = $0.0008/token):
  • Starter effective: $0.00072/token
  • Growth effective: $0.000656/token
  • Enterprise effective: $0.000576/token

- Overage: billed at 1.15x committed rate (i.e., small premium) with automated alerts at 80/95% thresholds.
- True-ups and credits: quarterly true-up; unused commit creditable within the 12-month contract only (no multi-year rollover) OR convertible to a one-time credit toward Redwood Optimize consulting (mutually exclusive).
- Additional terms: 30-day termination with pro-rata refunds on unused committed amounts for Starter/Growth; Enterprise requires 90-day notice.

Next steps I propose: confirm target tier and any specific SLAs (p50/p95 latency requirements, region pinning). I can loop in Marissa for commercial approval and Hannah for commercial legal on SOW language.

Attached: acme_commit_summary_v1.pdf; SOW_acme_draft.docx

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: RE: Exploring annual commit tiers and discounts for Hosted API

Looping in pricing/finance — quick notes from my side:

- The tier math looks clean; recommend we hold Growth at 1B (18%) but propose a 12-month performance rebate for Enterprise if usage exceeds committed volume by >10% for two consecutive quarters (protects Redwood unit economics).
- For Starter, propose a 6-month pilot addendum with option to upgrade to Growth at a pro-rated conversion rate (limits procurement friction).

Rishi — can you confirm margin impact on the proposed rebate and pilot terms? Hannah — please flag any procurement redlines in the SOW (especially around data residency and audit logs).

—Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Tim Carson <tim.carson@acme-payments.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@acme-payments.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted API Annual Commit: Volume discount proposal & packaging options

Tim / Sara —

Thanks for reviewing. Two small concessions we can offer to remove procurement friction:

1) 6-month pilot clause on Starter with an automatic pro-rated conversion to Growth on signature (no backdated true-up).
2) Doc-level security addendum for EU region (we'll include regional logging and KMS options in the SOW).

Marissa also asked for a conditional rebate for Enterprise if usage materially overshoots commit — proposed language:

  • If actual usage >110% of committed tokens for two consecutive quarters, Redwood will apply a 4% rebate on the overage volume applied to the next invoice (capped at 15% of annual committed spend).

If that sounds reasonable, we can push a DocuSign for the SOW + commit summary (link below) and set a March pricing window target to lock rates through year-end.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/templates/rdw-acme-commit

Can you confirm target tier this week? Happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize.

Jonas

From: Tim Carson <tim.carson@acme-payments.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.li@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 20:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted API Annual Commit: Volume discount proposal & packaging options

Jonas —

This looks good. Procurement wants Growth-level economics but an Enterprise-style rebate guardrail — they asked that the 1B Growth commit be the initial signature and we include the Enterprise rebate clause you proposed. Also want the 6-month pilot on Starter as a fallback (we may pilot a second product on that).

Please send the updated SOW with the two edits and the DocuSign. If we can get signature by Apr 6 we can align budget cycles.

I'll loop Legal if needed.

Thanks —
Tim
